about.whoWeAreFallback: We are a community of believers committed to worship, fellowship, and service.
about.beliefsIntro: While our full statement of faith is being prepared for publication, here is a summary of what we hold to be true.
about.beliefsItem1: We believe in one God, eternally existing in three persons: Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.
about.beliefsItem2: We believe the Bible is the inspired and authoritative Word of God.
about.beliefsItem3: We believe in salvation by grace through faith in Jesus Christ.
about.beliefsItem4: We believe in the power of prayer and the presence of the Holy Spirit in the life of every believer.
about.beliefsItem5: We believe the Church is the body of Christ, called to worship, fellowship, and serve one another.
about.historyBody: Our church's full history is being documented and will be published here soon. Every family, every service, and every milestone has shaped who we are today.
about.historyParagraph1: In 1995, a small gathering of believers began meeting for prayer and fellowship in a modest room, driven by a shared conviction that their community needed a place to worship, grow in faith, and support one another. What started as a handful of families meeting informally soon grew into a covenant of believers committed to building something lasting. Under the leadership of Fr. Emmanuel Mushi, our parish was formally established, and its first services were held with a simple altar, borrowed chairs, and an unwavering sense of purpose.
about.historyParagraph2: By the turn of the millennium, the congregation had outgrown its original meeting space. Fr. Joseph Kileo took up leadership in 1999 and guided the community through a season of steady growth, welcoming new families and establishing some of our earliest ministries. It was during this period that our first choir was formed, weekly Bible study groups began meeting in members' homes, and the foundations of our Jumuia small-group system were laid, a structure that continues to knit our congregation together today.
about.historyParagraph3: The years from 2003 to 2008, under the guidance of Fr. Anthony Mrema, saw the congregation take its most ambitious step yet: construction of a permanent worship building. Members gave generously of their time, skills, and resources, and volunteers spent countless weekends laying bricks and raising walls. When the doors finally opened, it was more than a building. It was a testament to what a community can accomplish when united by faith and purpose.
about.historyParagraph4: Fr. Peter Massawe's leadership from 2008 to 2013 brought a renewed focus on discipleship across every generation. Children's and youth ministries were formalized, a dedicated Sunday school curriculum was introduced, and the church's outreach extended into the surrounding community through visits to the sick, support for struggling families, and partnerships with local schools.
about.historyParagraph5: Between 2013 and 2018, Fr. Gabriel Ndosi oversaw further expansion of church facilities to accommodate the growing congregation, alongside a renewed emphasis on generosity and stewardship. It was during this time that our gallery of church memories began, capturing baptisms, weddings, and celebrations that have shaped our shared story.
about.historyParagraph6: The years from 2018 to 2022, guided by Fr. Vincent Shayo, tested the congregation's resilience as the wider world faced unprecedented challenges. Even so, the church adapted, strengthening its prayer ministries and finding new ways to stay connected as a family of faith through difficult seasons.
about.historyParagraph7: Since 2022, under the leadership of Fr. Michael Temba, our parish has continued to grow, with a renewed focus on evangelism, outreach, and equipping members to live out their faith in daily life. Today, more than three decades after that first small gathering in 1995, our church stands as a living testimony to what began as a handful of believers and grew into a family spanning generations, all still rooted in the same conviction that brought us together: that this is a place to belong, to grow, and to serve.

faq.intro: Answers to common questions from first-time visitors and our church family.
faq.q1: What should I wear to a service?
faq.a1: Come as you are. Most of our members dress comfortably and casually, though some prefer to dress up a little for Sunday service.
faq.q2: Is there a program for children?
faq.a2: Yes. Our Children's Ministry offers age-appropriate Bible teaching during our main services.
faq.q3: How do I get involved in a ministry?
faq.a3: Visit our Ministries page to see what's available, then speak with any of our leaders after a service or contact us to be connected.
faq.a4: We are working on making our services available online. Please check our News & Announcements section for updates.
faq.a5: Use our Prayer Request page to send your request directly and privately to our pastoral team.
faq.q6: How can I give or support the church?
faq.a6: Please contact us directly for information on how to give or support the church's ministries.
